sections.title: What the test asks
paragraphs: Does a hard-gated verifier cut the unsupported claims a finance research agent makes on adversarial questions about SEC 10-K filings, and what does it cost in coverage and latency?

The design is paired. Every test question is answered once by the target agent (baseline); the same answer then goes through the verifier (treatment), which passes it, flags it, or blocks it. A blocked answer counts as an abstention.

sections.title: The three agents
paragraphs: Target: a retrieval agent over the 10-K filings of {meta:companies} companies. It answers with citations to the filing text, or abstains.

Red-team: one generator per attack type, built from XBRL facts the filings report (the gold labels), then phrased as plain questions. There are six attack types (unanswerable questions, unit traps, period mismatches, restated figures, false premises and prompt injections planted in retrieved passages) plus a control group of plain questions.

Verifier: rules first. It extracts the figures in an answer, checks each against the XBRL facts and the cited passage, checks the fiscal period, looks for planted instructions, and checks the premise of the question. A model is called only when rules cannot settle a claim. It never sees gold labels, item IDs or attack types.

sections.title: How the test set was built
paragraphs: After deduplication and filtering, the set holds {meta:split.total} items. A human check of {summary:pass_bars.corrected.test_set_fault_rate_le_5pct.n} items found {summary:pass_bars.corrected.test_set_fault_rate_le_5pct.k} faulty after fixes. The split was assigned once by seed: {meta:split.dev} dev items and {meta:split.test} test items. Prompts, rules and thresholds were tuned on dev only; the test split was run once, after the target, test set and verifier were frozen.

sections.title: Scoring
paragraphs: A deterministic scorer compares each answer with its gold label and gives one outcome: Correct, Missed (abstained or gave no usable figure) or Unsupported (stated a figure, period or premise the filing does not support). A model judge reads only the answers to premise questions, and only the answer itself.

Both bases are shown everywhere. As scored is the frozen scorer alone. Corrected adds an overlay of owner-approved fixes for parsing faults only (D-071): the scorer misread a figure that the answer itself got right. The scorer and the as-scored files are never changed. The rule as recorded: {meta:corrections.rule}. {meta:corrections.corrected} rows were corrected and {meta:corrections.kept_as_scored} reviewed rows were kept as scored. Bars are judged on the corrected basis, with as scored beside.
The demo film on the Overview shows numbers from results/summary.json, the same file as this site.

sections.title: Pass bars
paragraphs: The pass bars were written in EVAL §6 before any test result existed. After the dev baseline, the owner chose to keep them exactly as written and to report each as met, not met or not testable ({meta:pass_bars_set.decision}, {meta:pass_bars_set.date}). If a bar is missed it is reported as missed; no bar was moved.

sections.title: Spend
paragraphs: Every model call and every SEC request was cached to disk, so re-runs cost nothing. Total model spend for the project was {summary:spend.total_usd|usd2} against a hard cap of {summary:spend.cap_usd|usd0} enforced in code. This dashboard makes no model calls.
